title: The creator of Walmart's vibe-coding tool Code Puppy is leaving for AI startup Pydantic
excerpt: The creator of Walmart's internal vibe-coding tool is leaving for AI start-up Pydantic. Code Puppy lets workers code their own software tools.
content_html:
Exclusive

By Dominick Reuter

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

The creator of Walmart's internal vibe-coding tool is leaving the company for AI start-up Pydantic.

In a memo reviewed by Business Insider, Michael Pfaffenberger wrote to colleagues that he was leaving Walmart a year after growing Code Puppy from 1,000 users to nearly 75,000. The tool will continue to be supported by his colleagues at Walmart.

Code Puppy, based on the Pydantic AI library, was created by Pfaffenberger, a distinguished engineer in Walmart's Global Tech group. The AI coding assistant helps developers write, edit, test, and manage software using natural-language instructions.

"I'm filled with joy that I was able to create software that improved the lives of so many folks at work and outside of it," Pfaffenberger wrote in the memo. "These decisions are never easy, but the time is right."

Walmart confirmed Pfaffenberger's departure and wished him the best. The company is in a quiet period ahead of its earnings report on August 20.

"People are using it in merchandising, people are using it in supply chain, store managers are using it. It's a way where the power of technology has now gotten democratized," chief technology officer Suresh Kumar said in June.

The company said in June that Code Puppy is now used by about as many non-engineers as there are engineers, all the way to hourly associates. One regional load manager used Code Puppy to design a tool that analyzes hundreds of available truckloads in the region to minimize truck drivers turning around after a dropoff without a load.

Code Puppy is part of Walmart's effort to avoid what many technology executives fear could become one of the defining business problems of the AI era: getting locked into a handful of powerful providers.

Like Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex, it can build features, fix bugs, and analyze projects. But unlike many rivals, Code Puppy isn't tied to a single AI model or provider.

Instead, it can work with dozens of models from different suppliers, allowing developers to switch between them, compare results, or use several at once. It can also distribute workloads across providers, helping avoid usage limits and control costs.

Walmart already has a dizzying number of agents and a handful of super-agents tailored for particular use cases, but Code Puppy was notable for its ability to help people across the organization vibe code their own solutions.

At the annual shareholders meeting last month, Pfaffenberger and his colleague John Choi received an award from CEO John Furner in recognition of the project.

Pydantic chief technology officer David Montague told Business Insider that Pfaffenberger is bringing his unique experience at a large enterprise building AI tools that coordinate multiple agents. This is a critical skill as large companies struggle with AI adoption, he added.

Read Pfaffenberger's memo to staff

Code Puppy is Staying

Friends, Walmartians, Vibe Coders,
A year ago today, Code Puppy barely had 1,000 total users. Now our lifetime user count, at the time of writing this email, is approaching 75,000. I'm filled with joy that I was able to create software that improved the lives of so many folks at work and outside of it.
This was not easy. I poured my soul into it for the past year. You kept me motivated. All of you, the users who felt empowered by the tool that I created, have been my lifeline and the reason I've kept going for so long.
Unfortunately, the time has come for me to say goodbye. These decisions are never easy, but the time is right.
With Brian Knapp's blessing, I was able to build a wonderful team. In my absence, these amazing folks will continue supporting and building on this project:

  • Ryan Eccles - Associate Fellow II
  • John Choi - Principal Software Engineer
  • Kaveri Bakshi - Director, Technical Program Management
  • Wesley Blakemore - Senior Software Engineer
  • Andrew Tilson - Principal Software Engineer
  • TJ Webb - Principal Software Engineer

Read more about them here: puppy.walmart.com/team
Together, they will uphold the tenets written here (puppy.walmart.com/tenets) and keep the project alive and well. I wrote these tenets recently, knowing that I would be gone soon. They are derived from the lessons in Made in America by Sam Walton, as well as the fundamental core of Walmart culture itself. Every team should follow them, not just this one.
And now that the team is up and running, I must say goodbye.
The decision to open source Code Puppy was pivotal. Code Puppy has been downloaded on the open source over 496,000 times, including 71,000+ times last month, by users all over the world. Dozens of individuals unaffiliated with Walmart have contributed powerful features and bug fixes. Because of this, it was almost like I had an entire team of elite software engineers - some of them folks at the absolute top of their fields, coming out of Stanford, like Qian Li (Founder of DBOS).
In September and October of last year, open source Code Puppy became heavily used in the Cerebras Discord when they launched their inference product. TJ Webb, a recent addition to the team, was one of those users. TJ has been contributing to Code Puppy the entire time - we just hired TJ last month.
github.com/mpfaffenberger/code_puppy is the open source version. You can use it on your machine at home. Do not use this version at Walmart, it won't work. Always use the internal one.
But please consider giving it a star on GitHub. This will attract more developers to maintain it when I'm gone.
And so here is my final release inside of Walmart, a culmination of over ~25 contributors and over 400 commits over the past month. Release notes below.
With gratitude, and bark mode activated one last time, thanks to all of you, sincerely, from the bottom of my heart,
Michael Pfaffenberger
Creator, Code Puppy

Correction: August 3, 2026 — An earlier version of this story misstated the number of Code Puppy users at Walmart. There are nearly 75,000 users.

But please consider giving it a star on GitHub. This will attract more developers to maintain it when I'm gone.
And so here is my final release inside of Walmart, a culmination of over ~25 contributors and over 400 commits over the past month. Release notes below.
With gratitude, and bark mode activated one last time, thanks to all of you, sincerely, from the bottom of my heart,
Michael Pfaffenberger
Creator, Code Puppy

独家的

作者：Dominick Reuter 您目前正在关注该作者！ 想要取消关注吗？ 通过电子邮件中的链接取消订阅。

沃尔玛内部振动编码工具的创建者即将离开公司，加入人工智能初创公司 Pydantic。

在 Business Insider 审阅的一份备忘录中，Michael Pfaffenberger 在给同事的信中表示，在 Code Puppy 用户从 1,000 名增加到近 75,000 名用户一年后，他将离开沃尔玛。 该工具将继续得到他在沃尔玛的同事的支持。

Code Puppy 基于 Pydantic AI 库，由沃尔玛全球科技团队的杰出工程师 Pfaffenberger 创建。 AI 编码助手帮助开发人员使用自然语言指令编写、编辑、测试和管理软件。

普法芬伯格在备忘录中写道：“我非常高兴能够开发出能够改善许多人工作内外生活的软件。” “这些决定从来都不容易，但时机已经成熟。”

沃尔玛证实了普法芬伯格的离职，并祝他一切顺利。 在 8 月 20 日发布收益报告之前，该公司正处于安静期。

“人们在销售中使用它，人们在供应链中使用它，商店经理也在使用它。 这是技术力量现在变得民主化的一种方式，”首席技术官苏雷什·库马尔 (Suresh Kumar) 在 6 月份表示。

该公司在 6 月份表示，目前使用 Code Puppy 的非工程师数量与工程师数量相当，一直到小时工。 一位区域负载经理使用 Code Puppy 设计了一种工具，可以分析该地区数百辆可用的卡车负载，以最大程度地减少卡车司机在空载下车后掉头的情况。

Code Puppy 是沃尔玛努力避免许多技术高管担心可能成为人工智能时代的决定性业务问题之一的努力的一部分：被少数强大的提供商所束缚。

与 Anthropic 的 Claude Code 和 OpenAI 的 Codex 一样，它可以构建功能、修复错误和分析项目。 但与许多竞争对手不同的是，Code Puppy 并不依赖于单一的人工智能模型或提供商。

相反，它可以与来自不同供应商的数十种模型配合使用，允许开发人员在它们之间切换、比较结果或同时使用多个模型。 它还可以跨提供商分配工作负载，帮助避免使用限制并控制成本。

沃尔玛已经拥有数量惊人的代理和一些针对特定用例量身定制的超级代理，但 Code Puppy 因其帮助整个组织内的人员编写自己的解决方案的能力而闻名。

在上个月的年度股东大会上，Pfaffenberger 和他的同事 John Choi 获得了首席执行官 John Furner 颁发的奖项，以表彰该项目。

Pydantic 首席技术官 David Montague 告诉《商业内幕》，Pfaffenberger 正在带来他在一家大型企业构建协调多个代理的人工智能工具的独特经验。 他补充说，这是一项关键技能，因为大公司在人工智能的采用方面举步维艰。

朋友们，沃尔玛人，Vibe Coders，一年前的今天，Code Puppy 的用户总数还只有 1,000 名。 现在，在撰写本电子邮件时，我们的终身用户数量已接近 75,000 人。 我很高兴能够创建软件来改善许多人在工作中和工作之外的生活。这并不容易。 在过去的一年里，我全身心地投入其中。 你让我充满动力。 你们所有人，那些因我创建的工具而感到强大的用户，一直是我的生命线，也是我坚持这么久的原因。不幸的是，现在是我说再见的时候了。 这些决定绝非易事，但时机成熟。在布莱恩·纳普 (Brian Knapp) 的支持下，我能够组建一支出色的团队。 在我缺席的情况下，这些了不起的人们将继续支持和建设这个项目：

  • 瑞恩·埃克尔斯 (Ryan Eccles) - II 级副研究员
  • John Choi - 首席软件工程师
  • Kaveri Bakshi - 技术项目管理总监
  • Wesley Blakemore - 高级软件工程师
  • Andrew Tilson - 首席软件工程师
  • TJ Webb - 首席软件工程师

在这里阅读有关他们的更多信息：puppy.walmart.com/teamTogether，他们将秉承此处写下的原则 (puppy.walmart.com/tenets) 并保持项目的活力和良好发展。 我最近写下了这些信条，因为我知道我很快就会离开。 它们源自萨姆·沃尔顿《美国制造》的教训，以及沃尔玛文化本身的基本核心。 每个团队都应该遵循他们，而不仅仅是这个团队。现在团队已经成立并正在运行，我必须说再见。开源 Code Puppy 的决定至关重要。 Code Puppy 的开源下载次数已超过 496,000 次，其中上个月被世界各地的用户下载了 71,000 多次。 数十名与沃尔玛无关的个人贡献了强大的功能和错误修复。 正因为如此，我几乎拥有了一整支精英软件工程师团队 - 其中一些人是各自领域的绝对顶尖人才，来自斯坦福大学，比如李干（DBOS 创始人）。去年 9 月和 10 月，开源 Code Puppy 在推出推理产品时在 Cerebras Discord 中得到了大量使用。 最近加入该团队的 TJ Webb 就是这些用户之一。 TJ 一直在为 Code Puppy 做出贡献 - 我们上个月刚刚聘请了 TJ。github.com/mpfaffenberger/code_puppy 是开源版本。 您可以在家里的机器上使用它。 不要在沃尔玛使用这个版本，它不起作用。 始终使用内部的。但请考虑在 GitHub 上给它一颗星。 当我离开后，这将吸引更多的开发人员来维护它。这是我在沃尔玛内部的最终版本，是过去一个月超过 25 名贡献者和超过 400 次提交的成果。 发布说明如下。带着感激之情，最后一次激活吠叫模式，衷心感谢你们所有人，Michael Pfaffenberger创始人，Code Puppy
